skills.name: Reciprocal & quotient identities
skills.wrong_turn: tan θ is sin θ/cos θ, not cos θ/sin θ; that's cot θ. And sec θ = 1/cos θ, not 1/sin θ.

skills.name: Pythagorean identities
skills.wrong_turn: It is 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, not 1 − tan²θ. And sin²θ means (sin θ)², not sin(θ²).

skills.name: Simplify trig expressions
skills.wrong_turn: Don't cancel across a sum. (sin x + cos x)/cos x is tan x + 1, not sin x.
skills.rule: Rewrite in sin and cos, factor, combine fractions, use identities, cancel.

skills.name: Prove identities
skills.wrong_turn: Don't work both sides toward the middle with non-reversible steps like squaring. Transform one side until it matches the other.
skills.rule: Work on one side only, until it matches the other.

skills.name: Sum & difference formulas
skills.wrong_turn: sin(A + B) is not sin A + sin B. sin(30° + 60°) = 1, but sin 30° + sin 60° ≈ 1.37.

skills.name: Double-angle formulas
skills.wrong_turn: sin 2A is not 2 sin A. sin 60° ≈ 0.87, but 2 sin 30° = 1.

skills.name: Half-angle formulas
skills.wrong_turn: Don't keep both signs. Choose from the quadrant of A/2: for A = 300°, A/2 = 150°, so cos(A/2) is negative.

skills.name: Harmonic form

steps.a: R and α from a and b
steps.b: a cos θ + b sin θ = R cos(θ − α)

skills.wrong_turn: sin A cos B is not sin(AB) or ½ sin(A + B). Both terms are needed: ½[sin(A + B) + sin(A − B)].

skills.name: Basic trig equations
skills.wrong_turn: The calculator gives one answer. sin x = 0.5 has x = 150° as well as 30°.
skills.rule: Isolate the function, find the reference angle, then take every quadrant where the sign fits.

skills.name: Intervals & general solutions
skills.wrong_turn: Add the period to every solution, not just one. sin x = 1/2 gives π/6 + 2πk and 5π/6 + 2πk.
skills.rule: Solve over one period, then add 2πk (or πk for tangent) to get every solution.

skills.name: Equations by factoring & identities
skills.wrong_turn: Never divide both sides by sin x or cos x: you lose the solutions where it is zero. Factor instead.
skills.rule: Get zero on one side, factor, and set each factor to zero; use identities to reach a single function.

skills.name: Multiple-angle equations
skills.wrong_turn: Don't solve over one turn and stop. sin 2x = k on [0, 2π) usually has four solutions, not two.
skills.rule: For sin2x=k on [0,2π), solve for u=2x on [0,4π), then halve.
